ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r2.claim: The arrogant Quraysh leader fashioned a disdainfully delivered excuse, misjudging the Qur’an as a prophet’s stirring eloquence and ignoring its warning, though its statements are realities he will soon meet.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r2.anchor: they reckoned it to be a miracle of a prophet’s stirring and eloquent speech and never paid attention to its warning

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p45/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p45/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p45/r3.claim: The Qur'an depicts his arrogance: he assesses listeners' moods, frowns to signal a hopeless judgment, then turns away muttering.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p45/r3.anchor: he lifted his face assessing the faces of the people

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r2.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r2.claim: The frowning and scowling may show al-Walīd's options had run out, or describe his expression toward the Prophet; turning away can be physical or a departure from truth, and arrogance may mean haughtiness toward truth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r2.anchor: ثم عبس وبسر: أي قطب وكلح لما ضاقت عليه الحيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān treats these gestures as satirical signs of fabrication: a truthful judgment would bring visible joy and need no strained, delayed deliberation; another view says he considered the Qurʾān's proofs before frowning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r3.anchor: وصفه بالهيئات التي تشكل بها حين أراد أن يقول: ما قال كل ذلك على سبيل الاستهزاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r4.claim: The conjunctions distinguish related acts: frowning and scowling are near-synonyms, arrogance causes turning away, while the fāʾ signals his immediate utterance after forming the charge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r4.anchor: وكان العطف في وبسر وفي واستكبر، لأن البسور قريب من العبوس

ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n11/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n11/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n11/r1.claim: Asad directs readers to 96:6-7 for comparison.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p124#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p124#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p124#4/r1.claim: He turned away from the truth—or from the Messenger—and arrogantly refused to follow him.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p124#4/r1.anchor: ثم أدبر عن الحق أو عن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم واستكبر عن اتباعه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r7.claim: Although reflection led him toward faith in the Qur’an’s soundness, he turned away from that conclusion and proudly refused to acknowledge the truth.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r7.anchor: عما أداه إليه فكره من الإيمان بسلامة المنظور فيه وعلوه عن المطاعن

BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r8.claim: His conceit was extreme: he brought himself to reject the truth even though he was in great need of acknowledging it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r8.anchor: وأوجد الكبر عن الاعتراف بالحق إيجاد من هو في غاية الرغبة فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r1.claim: The successive actions coordinate with “devised”; the sequence is a rise in rank, not time, because all occurred during his thinking and planning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r1.anchor: وهي ارتقاء متوالل فيما اقتضى التعجيب من حاله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r5.claim: One possible metaphor is that he abandoned his effort to devise a description for the Qur’an in despair, then turned to arrogant disdain.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r5.anchor: يجوز أن يكون مستعارا لتغيير التفكير الذي كان يفكره ويقدره يأسا من أن يجد ما فكر في انتحاله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, “turned away” may mean that he increasingly rejected belief in the Prophet, as Pharaoh is described turning away.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مستعارا لزيادة إعراضه عن تصديق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r7.claim: The successive expressions satirically portray al-Walīd’s contortions as he strained to invent a description for the Qur’an.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r7.anchor: وصفت أشكاله التي تشكل بها لما أجهد نفسه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407/r1.claim: He turned away from faith and acted arrogantly when called to it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407/r1.anchor: ثم أدبر عن الإيمان واستكبر أي تكبر حين دعي إليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r6.claim: Al-Walid turned from truth and retreated arrogantly, refusing to submit to the Quran.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r6.anchor: وقوله: {ثم أدبر واستكبر} أي: صرف عن الحق، ورجع القهقرى مستكبرا عن الانقياد للقرآن،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r9.claim: The man is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi, a Quraysh leader.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r9.anchor: وهذا المذكور في هذا السياق هو: الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي، أحد رؤساء قريش

NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#12/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#12/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#12/r1.claim: He turned away from the truth.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#12/r1.anchor: ﴿ ثم أدبر ﴾ عن الحق ﴿ واستكبر ﴾ عنه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#12/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#12/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#12/r2.claim: He arrogantly rejected the truth, or acted proudly regarding his own status and speech.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#12/r2.anchor: عنه أو عن مقامه وفي مقاله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#12/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#12/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#12/r3.claim: “Then he looked” is coordinated with “he thought and plotted”; the curse is parenthetical, and repeated thumma marks the delay between actions.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#12/r3.anchor: ثم نظر عطف على فكر وقدر والدعاء اعتراض بينهما وايراد ثم المعطوفات لبيان أن بين الأفعال المعطوفة تراخيا

QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r6.claim: Al-Walid turned away and went to his family.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r6.anchor: { ثم أدبر } أي ولى وأعرض ذاهبا إلى أهله.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r7.claim: He was too arrogant to believe.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r7.anchor: { واستكبر } أي تعظم عن أن يؤمن.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r8.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r8.claim: Another view says he turned away from faith and became arrogant when invited to it.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r8.anchor: وقيل: أدبر عن الإيمان واستكبر حين دعي إليه.

RAZI-FULL:v30p178/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p178/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p178/r1.claim: He turned away from the rest of the people toward his family, and arrogantly refused to believe.
RAZI-FULL:v30p178/r1.anchor: أدبر عن سائر الناس إلى أهله واستكبر أي تعظم عن الإيمان

RAZI-FULL:v30p178/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p178/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p178/r2.claim: The fāʾ marks immediate sequence: after turning away in pride, he voiced this objection.
RAZI-FULL:v30p178/r2.anchor: وإنما ذكره بفاء التعقيب ليعلم أنه لما ولى واستكبر ذكر هذه الشبهة

TAB-FULL:v23p432/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p432/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p432/r1.claim: He turned away from faith and belief in God's revelation, arrogantly refusing the truth; he claimed the Qur'an was magic taken from another person.
TAB-FULL:v23p432/r1.anchor: ثم ولى عن الإيمان والتصديق بما أنزل الله من كتابه، واستكبر عن الإقرار بالحق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r1.claim: He turned away toward his family as a denier.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r2.claim: He arrogantly held himself above accepting faith.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r3.claim: Muqatil says he turned away from faith and grew arrogant when invited to it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل: أدبر عن الإيمان (¬11)، وتكبر حين دعي إليه

STUDYQURAN:74:11/r23.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r23.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r23.claim: Turning his back means al-Walīd rejected faith and affirming the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r23.anchor: al-Walīd turned his back, that is, on faith and the verification of the Quran

STUDYQURAN:74:11/r24.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r24.speaker: Ṭ, JJ
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r24.claim: Istakbara is read with an implied ʿan (“from”), so it means he disdained to affirm the truth or scorned the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r24.anchor: the preposition does not occur here, many consider it to be implied

TABATABAI:74:12-25/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r10.claim: The sequence portrays al-Walid after deliberation: he looks to judge, frowns and shows disgust, then turns away and grows arrogant before speaking.
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r10.anchor: تمثيل لحاله بعد التكفير والتقدير وهو من ألطف التمثيل وأبلغه

TABATABAI:74:12-25/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r13.claim: Turning away and pride are inner states sequenced after visible facial states because they become evident in his words; fa links his words to those attitudes, not thumma.
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r13.anchor: والأمران أعني الإدبار والاستكبار من الأحوال الروحية، وإنما رتبا في التمثيل على النظر والعبوس

BURSEVI:v10p178/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p178/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p178/r1.claim: He turned from truth, arrogantly refused to follow it, and then spoke.

TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r24.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r24.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r24.claim: He turned away from faith and acted arrogantly when called to it.
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r24.anchor: عن الإيمان { واستكبر } أي تكبر حين دعا إليه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:21-27/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:21-27/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:21-27/r3.claim: He turned away and grew arrogant toward faith.

ELMALILI:74:14-25/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r17.claim: He turned from the truth, turned his back on faith toward unbelief, and arrogantly refused to acknowledge the truth.
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r17.anchor: anlamış olduğu haktan yüz çevirdi, imana arkasını, küfre yüzünü döndürdü ve Allah’tan korkmayıp gurur ile büyüklük tasladı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r3.claim: Verses 18–25 condemn people who, like al-Walīd, adopt a similar unbelieving posture toward the Qur’an.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r3.anchor: İşte 18-25. âyetlerde Velîd b. Mug^re örneğinde Kur’an’a karşı benzer şekilde inkârcı tutum sergileyenler kınanmış

NAHHAS:v5p67/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p67/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p67/r6.claim: He turned away from truth and arrogantly refused belief after preparing to refute the signs, although he did not disdain bowing to powerless stones.
NAHHAS:v5p67/r6.anchor: عن الحق ( واستكبر ) فأخبر الله بجهله أنه تكبر أن يصدق بآيات الله ورسوله

ASAD-NOTES:74:16/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:16/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:16/r3.claim: On hearing the messages, he reflects on how to disprove them, destroys himself by that deliberation, looks for arguments, frowns, then turns away and glories in arrogance.
ASAD-NOTES:74:16/r3.anchor: he reflects and meditates [as to how to disprove them]

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p269/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p269/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p269/r7.claim: He turned away from faith and became arrogant when invited to it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p269/r7.anchor: {ثم أدبر} عن الإيمان {واستكبر} تكبر حين دعي إليه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:20-28/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:20-28/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:20-28/r5.claim: He turned away from the truth or the Messenger and arrogantly refused to follow.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:20-28/r5.anchor: عن الحق أو الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام. { واستكبر } عن اتباعه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r6.claim: If the curse praises his first judgment, al-Walid reconsidered the Quran, saw Muhammad's superior rank, frowned from envy, then turned away in pride and called it magic.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r6.anchor: نظر فيما احتج به القرآن فرأى ما فيه من علو مرتبة محمد عليه السلام

JISHUMI:v10p7156/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r9.claim: Idbār means turning rearward, opposite turning forward; tadabbur considers an outcome.
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r9.anchor: والإدبار: الأخذ على جهة الدبر، ونقيضه: الإقبال. دبر يدبر دبورا، وأدبر إدبارا،

JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.claim: The passage is said to concern al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi, wealthy with sons and called al-Wahid among his people, according to Ibn Amir.
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.anchor: قيل: نزلت هذه الآيات في الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي، وكان له مال وبنون، قال ابن عامر: وكان يسمى الوحيد في قومه،

JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.claim: In the story, al-Walid rejects calling Muhammad a soothsayer, poet, or madman, then chooses “magician” and says the Qur’an separates families.
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.anchor: ثم اختلفوا، فقيل: إنه أتى قريشا في ناديها، وقال: هذا الموسم، والناس يسألون عن محمد،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r14.claim: He turned away from the truth and arrogantly rejected it before making his accusation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r14.anchor: عن الحق { واستكبر } عنه فقال ما قال

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r2.speaker: السدي وتوبة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r2.claim: Al-Suddi glosses busur as changed; the line attributed to Tuba illustrates the term for altered, rejecting manner.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r2.anchor: الثاني : تغير , قاله السدي , ومنه قول توبة : وقد رابني منها صدود رأيته … وإعراضها عن حاجتي وبسورها

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r3.claim: Al-Mawardi suggests al-Walid may have frowned and scowled at the Prophet when the Prophet called him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r3.anchor: واحتمل أن يكون قد عبس وبسر على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حين دعاه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r4.claim: Alternatively, he may have scowled at those who believed in and supported the Prophet.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r4.anchor: واحتمل أن يكون على من آمن به ونصره .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r5.claim: The text distinguishes scowling that appears after conversation from scowling that appears before it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r5.anchor: وقيل إن ظهور العبوس في الوجه يكون بعد المحاورة , وظهور البسور في الوجه قبل المحاورة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r6.claim: One explanation is that he turned away from the truth and became arrogant toward obedience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r6.anchor: أحدهما : أدبر عن الحق واستكبر عن الطاعة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r7.claim: Another explanation is that he physically left his place and spoke arrogantly.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r7.anchor: الثاني : أدبر عن مقامه واستكبر في مقاله .

MUQATIL:74:18-30/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:18-30/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:18-30/r6.claim: Al-Walid turned away arrogantly and called the Qur'an transmitted magic and human speech.
MUQATIL:74:18-30/r6.anchor: { ثم أدبر واستكبر فقال إن هذآ إلا سحر يؤثر إن هذآ إلا قول البشر سأصليه سقر } [آية: 26]
